description: Phase-COMPOSITE — meta-tools che incorporano workflow comuni, riducendo la surface dei tool primitivi che l'LLM vede. Pattern lifted da D:/tmp/graphify/graphify/serve.py: UN tool MCP `query_graph` ritorna risposta completa, l'agente non orchestra nulla. Applicato ad Aura: 5 meta-tool che sostituiscono i pattern multi-call più frequenti (find_in_sources, extract_records, create_file_from_data, summarize_source, plus wiki_subgraph già esistente). Trigger 2026-05-21 dopo conferma live (turn 4715-4717): Aura riceve 'Trova un cliente e stampalo' su xlsx 90 righe, usa execute_code per leggere tutto, poi dumpa wall-of-text 36s. Phase-DISCIPLINE (in flight) caps il dump LATO TOOL; questa fase RIDUCE la randomness di tool selection mostrando all'LLM meno tool ma più potenti. DIPENDE da Phase-DISCIPLINE: Tool struct con OutputCap field + boundOutput wrapper + tool-description style già canonicalizzati. Eseguire DOPO Phase-DISCIPLINE chiusa. STRICT one-story-exit per scripts/ralph/CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: extract_records — meta-tool that filters source rows without LLM round-trips
userStories.description: Replace the (source + execute_code + LLM-filter) chain with one tool that reads a structured source's rows, filters by criteria, and returns ≤limit rows in a clean envelope. (a) NEW TOOL internal/agent/tools/registry/extract_records.go: ExtractRecordsTool. Parameters: source_id (required), criteria (object, optional — keys are column names, values are exact/contains/regex match), limit (int, default 10, max 50), columns (optional []string — project only these columns). (b) EXECUTE: (i) fetch source via internal/storage/sources/store; (ii) parse extract.md — leverage the structured frontmatter from Wave B B03/B08* plugins (sheet_row_counts / slide_count / heading_counts / row markers ###); (iii) for tabular sources (xlsx/csv): split on `### Row N` headings, parse `- col: value` bullets; (iv) apply criteria filter (each entry = AND match); (v) return JSON envelope `{source_id, total_matches, returned, rows:[{col:val,...}], next_cursor:''}`. (c) NON-TABULAR FALLBACK: if extract.md has no `### Row N` markers, return error 'source is not tabular; use find_in_sources or summarize_source instead'. (d) BOUNDS: respect OutputCap from US-DRIFT-02 (default 8 KiB stays, but the envelope structure tends to fit since each row is ~100 chars × 10 rows = 1 KB). (e) DESC: 'Read-only. Returns top-{limit} rows from a tabular source matching criteria. Use this INSTEAD of execute_code on Python DataFrames. Use for: "Trova il cliente X", "Quali righe hanno colonna Y = Z", "Mostrami i primi N".' (f) TEST: TestExtractRecords_TabularXlsx_FiltersByCriteria, TestExtractRecords_NonTabularFails, TestExtractRecords_LimitCapsResults, TestExtractRecords_RegisterAndExecute. (g) AGENT.md (runtime + defaults) gains a bullet in the existing 'Stile risposta' section: 'Per filtri su file tabulari (xlsx/csv) usa extract_records, NON execute_code.' (h) registry_scan_test adds extract_records to expected catalog.

(4) Read US-DRIFT-02 output (boundOutput wrapper) so the envelope respects OutputCap. PARSE DISCIPLINE: regex-only parsing of extract.md — `^### Row (\d+)$` for row boundaries, `^- (\w+): (.+)$` for cell bullets. Skip headings that aren't `### Row` (e.g., `## Sheet:`). FILTER MATCHING: exact-match string compare default; if criteria value is a map with 'contains' / 'regex' key, use that. Case-insensitive by default (most user queries are). Italian diacritic-strip via stringx (already exists in Aura). PAGINATION: v0 is single-page — next_cursor='' always. v1 can add real cursors. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: ONLY tabular extract. NO xlsx file generation here — that's US-COMP-04. NO new sources, NO ingest changes. INVARIANT: if extract.md has 0 matches, return total_matches=0, rows=[], no error.

userStories.title: find_in_sources — meta-tool that searches across ingested sources without LLM round-trips
userStories.description: Replace the (search_memory + read_source + LLM-search) chain with one tool that does FTS5+vector hybrid retrieval over the source corpus and returns top-N synthesized chunks. (a) NEW TOOL internal/agent/tools/registry/find_in_sources.go: FindInSourcesTool. Parameters: query (required string), source_id (optional — scope to ONE source), top_k (default 5, max 10). (b) EXECUTE: (i) call the wiki hybrid search backend that already serves search_memory — leverage compact_memory_fts + the recent fix(search) commit c7a82f1c for stop-word handling; (ii) filter results by kind=source (and optionally source_id) — kind already in the FTS5 schema; (iii) return JSON envelope `{query, total_hits, returned, chunks:[{source_id, snippet:..., score, byte_offset}], suggestion?: 'Use extract_records for tabular filter OR summarize_source for narrative summary'}`. (c) SUGGESTION FIELD: empty by default; populated when the chunks span >3 sources (suggesting the user should narrow). (d) DESC: 'Read-only. Returns top-{top_k} chunks across ingested sources matching {query}. Use for: "Cosa dice il documento X su Y", "Cerca menzioni di Z". Use INSTEAD of search_memory when the answer is in user-uploaded sources.' (e) AGENT.md bullet: 'Per cercare in file caricati usa find_in_sources, NON search_memory (che è per la wiki). search_memory rimane per pagine wiki create da Aura.' (f) TEST: TestFindInSources_HappyPath, TestFindInSources_ScopedToSourceID, TestFindInSources_SuggestsNarrowingOnManySources, TestFindInSources_RegisterAndExecute.

userStories.title: summarize_source — meta-tool that returns a structured source summary without dumping
userStories.description: Replace the (read_source + execute_code dump + LLM summarize) chain with one tool that reads extract.md, parses structure, and returns a compact bullet summary. (a) NEW TOOL internal/agent/tools/registry/summarize_source.go: SummarizeSourceTool. Parameters: source_id (required), focus (optional string — narrows the summary to that aspect, e.g., 'autori' or 'tabella vendite'), max_bullets (default 7, max 12). (b) EXECUTE: (i) fetch source + extract.md via internal/storage/sources/store; (ii) read frontmatter (sheets, slides, chapters, heading_counts from Wave B plugins); (iii) sample first paragraph + last paragraph + 3 middle blocks; (iv) call LLM with a TIGHT prompt asking for max_bullets bullets summarizing the source (or aspect if focus set), bullet ≤25 words each, in Italian. (v) Return JSON envelope `{source_id, structure:{kind, total_chunks, heading_count}, bullets:[...], focus_applied: bool}`. (c) DETERMINISTIC: temperature=0 for the LLM call. (d) SCOPE: structure-aware — for tabular sources (xlsx), bullets describe COLUMNS + sample values; for narrative (epub/html), bullets describe THEMES + key entities; for slides (pptx), bullets describe AGENDA. (e) DESC: 'Read-only. Returns ≤{max_bullets} bullets summarizing a source (optionally focused on a specific aspect). Use for: "Di cosa parla X", "Riassumi il documento Y". Use INSTEAD of execute_code + raw dump.' (f) TEST: TestSummarizeSource_TabularReturnsColumns, TestSummarizeSource_NarrativeReturnsThemes, TestSummarizeSource_FocusApplies, TestSummarizeSource_RegisterAndExecute.

(2) Read internal/llm/client.go (or similar) for the LLM Stream/Send interface to make a side LLM call from a tool. SIDE LLM CALL DISCIPLINE: this tool fires an LLM call OUTSIDE the agent loop. The agent receives the BULLETS, not the raw chunks. Use a small model if possible (config flag MaxToolResultChars / similar); fall back to the main LLM. TEMPERATURE=0 for reproducibility. PROMPT TEMPLATE: keep it tight. Example: 'Riassumi questa fonte in ESATTAMENTE {N} bullet, ognuno ≤25 parole. {focus_clause}. Struttura: {kind} con {chunk_count} sezioni. Contenuto:\n{sample}.' userStories.title: create_file_from_data — meta-tool that filters records and creates an xlsx/docx/pdf in one call
userStories.description: Replace the (source + execute_code + doc xlsx) chain — the EXACT pattern that broke 2026-05-21 (Aura took 36s + dumped 90 rows for 'crea un file excel'). One tool that filters records (via extract_records logic) and emits a doc artifact. (a) NEW TOOL internal/agent/tools/registry/create_file_from_data.go: CreateFileFromDataTool. Parameters: format (required, enum: 'xlsx'|'docx'|'pdf'), source_id (required), criteria (optional, same shape as extract_records), columns (optional []string), output_filename (required string), title (optional, for docx/pdf — default = source filename basename). (b) EXECUTE: (i) reuse the extract_records logic to get filtered rows (call into the same helper used by US-COMP-01); (ii) call doc action={format} via the existing doc tool wiring — pass {sheets:[{name, rows:[{col:val,...}]}]} for xlsx; pass {blocks:[...]} for docx/pdf; (iii) verify the file lands at /workspace/{output_filename}; (iv) return JSON envelope `{format, output_path, row_count, source_id, summary: '90 righe, 4 colonne — top 10 visualizzate' }`. (c) NO LIMIT cap on the GENERATED file (doc tool already handles 10k rows). limit=0 here means ALL filtered rows. (d) DESC: 'Read+Write. Filters rows from a source AND creates the requested xlsx/docx/pdf in ONE call. Use for: "Crea un xlsx con i clienti di tipo X", "Genera un PDF riepilogo". Use INSTEAD of (source + execute_code + doc xlsx).' (e) TEST: TestCreateFileFromData_Xlsx_FilteredRows, TestCreateFileFromData_Docx_WithTitle, TestCreateFileFromData_NoCriteria_AllRows, TestCreateFileFromData_RegisterAndExecute.

userStories.title: Tool surface cleanup — hide primitive tools the LLM should NOT pick directly
userStories.description: After US-COMP-01..04 ship, the agent has 4 new meta-tools that cover the common workflows. To stop the LLM from STILL randomly picking execute_code / execute_shell, we need to either (a) hide them or (b) mark them as 'last-resort'. Pattern: cli-printing-press uses description markers ('Destructive.', 'Read-only.') to teach the LLM by description-shape. (a) UPDATE descriptions of the primitive tools that the meta-tools now cover: (i) execute_code → 'LAST RESORT. Computation only. Do NOT use to read sources (use find_in_sources / extract_records / summarize_source), do NOT use to create files (use create_file_from_data), do NOT use to dump output. If you cannot accomplish the goal with a meta-tool, then and only then call this.'; (ii) execute_shell → same LAST RESORT pattern with the same list of meta-tools to prefer first. (iii) source action=read → 'LAST RESORT. Returns raw source bytes. Prefer summarize_source / extract_records / find_in_sources for typical asks. Use this ONLY when the meta-tools fail.'; (iv) file action=read on workspace files → 'For wiki pages use wiki_subgraph or search_memory. For ingested sources use the meta-tools listed above. Direct file reads are for /workspace/ files NOT in the wiki/source surface.' (b) AGENT.md (runtime + defaults) gains a NEW section `## Selezione tool — preferenze fisse`: a 10-line table mapping intent → first-choice meta-tool, with primitives as fallback. (c) AGENT.md anti-pattern section gains: 'Chiamare execute_code per leggere/filtrare/sommare un source ingerito — VIETATO se esiste un meta-tool (extract_records, find_in_sources, summarize_source).' (d) NO new tools, NO removed tools, NO Execute() logic change — only description strings + AGENT.md prose. (e) DESCRIPTION AUDIT TEST from US-DRIFT-05 should still pass — extend it to verify the LAST RESORT prefix where applicable.
